title: Sharat Industries Ltd - 519397 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Sharat Industries FY26 revenue rose about 38% to Rs 524.7 crore and PAT about 60% to Rs 15.90 crore, while Q4 was hit by Middle East disruption and fishmeal costs.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a strong year on revenue and profit, with export revenue up about 23% and export volumes up about 8%. Q4 revenue grew about 25% YoY to Rs 117.24 crore, but margins were squeezed by the West Asia conflict, which forced rerouting of Middle East-bound shipments, higher logistics costs and inventory build-up, along with sharp fishmeal and soya price increases. US tariffs on Indian shrimp fell from up to 50% to 10% effective February 2026, and management is targeting FY27-28 export revenue of up to Rs 1,000 crore. Management framed the Q4 margin pressure as largely external and event-driven rather than a change in the underlying business.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: US and China make up roughly 40% of export portfolio; Russia, Southeast Asia, Europe and Middle East the remaining 60%. Value-added products were about 7-10% of export volume in FY26, with management hoping to double that share by volume if conditions normalise.

segments.name: Domestic / feed and farming
segments.commentary: Q4 is the start of stocking season in Andhra Pradesh farming, but sharp fishmeal and soya price increases hurt margins. Feed market share is sub 2%. Sales to Hyperpure began in Q4 FY26 with base products such as raw frozen shrimp.

segments.name: Processing
segments.commentary: Premium black tiger shrimp and new value-added products are a stated priority. A 1 MW captive solar plant is partly commissioned in Q4, with the balance due shortly.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term roadmap to FY27-28 targets annual export revenue of up to Rs 1,000 crore, via deeper Russia and China penetration, re-entry into the EU and a measured domestic and value-added build-out.
US exports expected to scale up significantly versus the last couple of years in FY27, but management is cautious and will revisit clarity around end of the quarter.
Value-added share of export volume hoped to double from 7-10% if export conditions normalise.
EU FTA expected to take effect over the rest of calendar 2026; benefits to accrue gradually.
Raw material prices and realisations expected to keep moving through the cycle; management hopes the fishmeal spike is temporary.
capex_capacity: 1 MW solar plant for captive consumption at processing division: partly commissioned in Q4 FY26, balance to be commissioned shortly.
Insect protein substitution for fishmeal in feed: pilot farming under way for over a year, with farm-level results described as encouraging.
Management aims to improve processing plant utilisation and unlock operating leverage via contract farming and asset-light merchant exports; slight utilisation improvement was seen in FY26.
No quantified capacity, utilisation percentage or capex amount was given.
demand_pricing: About 20 containers were planned for Middle East shipments in Q4; about half were rerouted on customer advice, about five were in transit and needed rescue by shipping liners, and the rest are held as inventory being reprocessed for alternate destinations.
US tariffs on Indian shrimp cut from up to 50% to 10% effective February 2026; US is about 35-40% of export value. No new US clients were added in FY26 due to tariff turbulence.
Russia: two new clients added in FY26. China: new black tiger shrimp product, about five customers worked with so far.
PD Curl control product (launched in Russia) delivers incremental EBITDA margin of more than 5% up to about 10% over base EBITDA, but volumes are low.
Indian shrimp exports are about Rs 50,000-55,000 crore; company share is 0.5-0.75%.
Fishmeal price spike attributed to global demand and heavy Indian exports; industry has petitioned government for relief.

qa_highlights.question: How much business was hit by the West Asia conflict, and have deferred orders been recovered?
qa_highlights.answer: About 20 containers were planned for Middle East in Q4; half were rerouted to other destinations, about five were in transit and needed safe handling at extra cost, and the remainder sit in inventory being reprocessed for other markets.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key drivers of the ~60% PAT growth versus EBITDA growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited export diversification (China black tiger shrimp via a partner processor), slightly higher capacity utilisation, and value-added products improving margins; geopolitical shocks would otherwise have allowed better margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PD Curl control product's potential and where can it go next?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental EBITDA margin of more than 5% up to about 10% over base; volumes are currently low, and management plans to add products to the Russian portfolio this year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the company's market shares?
qa_highlights.answer: Share of Indian shrimp exports is about 0.5%, ranging 0.5-0.75%; feed market share is sub 2%, described as a minority position.

qa_highlights.question: What is the value-added share of exports and the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added products were about 7-10% of export volume in FY26; the company hopes to double that share by volume if export conditions are normal.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company handling the fishmeal price increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Insect protein substitution is in pilot; some costs passed to contract farmers; the company aims for better export contracts with improved margins; industry has sought government relief.

risks_watch: Fishmeal and soya cost inflation, which hit Q4 margins and may persist.
Middle East conflict: inventory of rerouted cargo must be sold through alternate channels; logistics costs elevated.
Weather-related farm risk flagged for the rest of calendar 2026.
US demand normalisation and recession risk; tariff level sustainability.
EU FTA ratification timing across member states; benefit may take time.
Q4 seasonal softness and whether margins recover in the next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year numbers and long-term diversification, but cautious and somewhat non-committal on FY27 demand, the US recovery and the timing of fishmeal and EU benefits. Management repeatedly attributed the Q4 shortfall to external events.
key_quotes: We see this as a largely external event-driven impact rather than a change in the underlying business.
Tariffs on Indian shrimp, which had increased up to 50%, have now been reduced to 10% with effect from February 2026.
This reflects the operating leverage our integrated model generates over a full cycle, even when individual quarters see some turbulence.

financial_highlights.change: up approx. 38% vs Rs 380.5 crore in FY25

financial_highlights.value: Rs 4.06 (stated as Rs 4.06 crore in transcript)
